questions.question: Find the area of a rhombus whose side is 10 cm and the longest diagonal is 16 cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Side (s) = 10 cm and half of longest diagonal = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.

In a rhombus, diagonals bisect at 90°, forming right triangles with the side as hypotenuse.

Using Pythagorean triplet (6, 8, 10), the half of the other diagonal = 6 cm.

Length of second diagonal (d₂) = 6 × 2 = 12 cm.

Area of rhombus = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂ = 1/2 × 16 × 12 = 96 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side (s) = 10 cm

Diagonal 1 (d₁) = 16 cm

questions.question: The compound interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 11% p.a. for 2 years is Rs. 4642. Find its simple interest at the same rate and for the same period.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Compound Interest on a sum for 2 years at 11% p.a. = Rs.4642

**Formulas used:**

Compound Interest + Principal = Amount 

⇒ Amount = Principal × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate/100 × Time 

**Calculation:**

4642 + P = P × (1 + 11/100)²

⇒ 4642 = P × 111/100 × 111/100 - P 

⇒ 4642 = P(111/100 × 111/100 - 1)

⇒ 4642 = P(12321 - 10000)/10000

⇒ 4642 = P × 2321/10000 

⇒ P = 4642 × 10000/2321 

⇒ P = Rs.20000

**∴ Simple Interest = 20000 × 11/100 × 2 = Rs.4400**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Percentage MethodCompound interest and simple interest both are calculated on Principal. Effective rate percent of compound interest for 2 years = R + R + (R × R)/100 

⇒ 11 + 11 + (11 × 11)/100 

⇒ 22 + 1.21 = 23.21% 

Simple interest rate percent for 2 years = Rate % × Time = 11% × 2 = 22% 

23.21% of Principal = Rs.4642 

⇒ 22% of Principal = Rs.4642 × 22%/23.21% = Rs.4400 

**∴ The simple interest is Rs.4400.**

questions.question: Name the Buddhist text that comprises rules for monks.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Buddhist text that comprises rules for monks is **Vinaya Pitaka**.
 
• **Vinaya Pitaka** is the oldest and smallest of the** three sections** of the Buddhist canonical **Tipitaka (“Triple Basket”)** and the one that regulates monastic life and the daily affairs of **monks and nuns** according to rules attributed to the Buddha.
 
• **Vinaya Pitaka is the first of the Tripitaka** and it contains all the disciplinary rules of ecclesiastical acts and duties formulated by the Buddha himself for the conduct and **guidance of monks and nuns**.
 
• It consists of five books: **Parajika, Pachittiya, Mahavagga, Chullavagga, and Parivara**.
 
• **Vinaya Pitaka** tells that there were separate wings for both men and women in **Buddhist Sangha**. It tells how to behave with each other and within the society. **In Vinaya Pitaka, all the rules for Buddhist Sangha were written down**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Buddhist text**
 **Description**
 
 

 Tipitaka
 It **is the collection of primary Pali language texts** which form the doctrinal foundation of **Theravada Buddhism**. Together with the ancient commentaries, they constitute the complete body of classical Theravada texts.
 
 

 Sutta Pitaka
 
 
Sutta Pitaka is an extensive body of texts constituting the **basic doctrinal section of the Buddhist canon.**

 
 
 

 Abhidhamma Pitaka
 
 
**The Abhidhamma Pitaka** is a collection of canonical texts in the **Theravada Buddhist tradition**.

 
Together with the Vinaya Pitaka and the Sutta Pitaka, it comprises the Tipitaka, the "Three Baskets" of canonical Theravada Buddhist texts.

Mean b, d and f = 28

Mean = Sum of observations/No of observations 

**Calculation:**

Sum of a, b, c, d, e and f = 36 × 6 = 216

Sum of b, d and f = 28 × 3 = 84 

Sum of a, c and e = Sum(a, b, c, d, e, f) - Sum(b, d, f) 

⇒ 216 - 84 = 132

**∴ Mean of a, c and e = 132/3 = 44**

questions.question: The smallest six-digit number which is completely divisible by 4, 8, 12 and 16 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Smallest six-digit number which is divisible by 4, 8, 12 and 16.

**Concept:**

LCM (Lowest Common Multiple)

Dividend = Divisor × Quotient + Remainder 

**Calculation:**

LCM of 4, 8, 12 & 16 will be calculated by writing them as the product of their prime factors. 

4 = 2²

8 = 2³

12 = 2² × 3 

16 = 2⁴

So, LCM (4, 8, 12, 16) = 2⁴ × 3 = 48 

The smallest six-digit number is 100000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7838db06e8c3a17d0223ef481eadf176f4478802b5f755f68fb3fdabb4ae4806.png] 

By dividing 100000 by 48, we get the remainder 16. 

So, we need to add the difference between the Divisor and Remainder to 100000 (Dividend) in order to get the smallest six-digit number divisible by 48.

⇒ 100000 + (48 - 16) = 48 × 2083 + 16 + (48 - 16) 

⇒ 100032 = 48 × 2083 + 16 + 32 

⇒ 100032 = 48 × 2083 + 48 

⇒ 100032 = 48 × 2083 + 48 

**∴ The smallest six-digit number which is completely divisible by 4, 8, 12 and 16 is 100032.**

questions.question: Find the sum of the numbers between 400 and 600 such that when they are divided by 6, 12 and 16, there will be no remainder.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required numbers must be exactly divisible by the LCM of 6, 12, and 16, which is 48.

Multiples of 48 between 400 and 600 are 48 × 9, 48 × 10, 48 × 11, and 48 × 12.

Required Sum = 48 × (9 + 10 + 11 + 12)

Required Sum = 48 × 42 = 2016

**∴ The correct answer is 2016.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 6, 12, and 16

Range = Numbers strictly between 400 and 600

**Concept Used:**

A number is exactly divisible by a set of given numbers if it is a multiple of their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 6 = 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 16 = 2⁴

⇒ LCM(6, 12, 16) = 2⁴ × 3 = 16 × 3 = 48

⇒ We need to find all multiples of 48 that lie between 400 and 600.

⇒ Dividing 400 by 48, we get a quotient of 8.

⇒ The first multiple greater than 400 = 48 × 9 = 432

⇒ The maximum multiple less than 600 = 48 × 12 = 576

⇒ The valid numbers are: 432, 480, 528, 576

⇒ Sum of these numbers = 432 + 480 + 528 + 576 = 2016

**∴ The correct answer is 2016.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is uniformly divisible by two or more numbers. It is obtained by taking the highest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.

Sum of Arithmetic Progression (A.P.)

Consecutive multiples of a number always form an Arithmetic Progression. The sum can also be calculated using the formula: Sₙ = n ÷ 2 × (first term + last term). Here, 4 ÷ 2 × (432 + 576) = 2 × 1008 = 2016.

Divisibility Rule

For a number to leave no remainder when divided by a group of divisors, it must be completely divisible by their LCM. If a remainder 'R' is specified, the general format of the number becomes (LCM × k) + R.
